notes: τῆς follows its noun ζωῆς and its modifier is a prepositional phrase, so rule 31's carve-out applies: the determiner stays on the noun (supplied there because ζωῆς is anarthrous) and the article keeps only which, with the copula on ἐν. This is the configuration the carve-out names, not the participle case of 1:9 and 1:14.
θελήματος, ἐπαγγελίαν and ἀπόστολος are all anarthrous, so each supplied determiner is a rule 51 helper on the noun it determines; no article competes for any of them.
